\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{آرامگاه} (ârâmgâh)}{آرامگاه (ârâmgâh)}]{\fa{آرامگاه} (ârâmgâh) — a tomb, a mausoleum}

\label{lesson:FA-C231-aramgah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for straight ahead, then the Persian for opposite.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{آرامگاه}}
\textbf{\fa{آرامگاه}} — \emph{ârâmgâh} — \textquotedblleft{}a tomb, a mausoleum\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ârâmgâh} is \emph{ârâm}, \textquotedblleft{}rest\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{gâh}, \textquotedblleft{}place\textquotedblright{}: the resting place. Both are native Persian; \emph{ârâm} is usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{ārām}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for straight ahead, then the Persian for opposite, then say \emph{ârâmgâh} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{وطن} (vatan)}{وطن (vatan)}]{\fa{وطن} (vatan) — homeland}

\label{lesson:FA-C231-vatan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a hall, then the Persian for a swimming pool.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{وطن}}
\textbf{\fa{وطن}} — \emph{vatan} — \textquotedblleft{}homeland\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{vatan} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{waṭan}, \textquotedblleft{}homeland, place of residence\textquotedblright{}. Its Arabic root is \emph{w-ṭ-n} (Lane).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{زادگاه} (zâdgâh)}{زادگاه (zâdgâh)}]{\fa{زادگاه} (zâdgâh) — birthplace}

\label{lesson:FA-C231-zadgah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a swimming pool, then the Persian for homeland.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{زادگاه}}
\textbf{\fa{زادگاه}} — \emph{zâdgâh} — \textquotedblleft{}birthplace\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{zâdgâh} is built from \emph{zâd}, \textquotedblleft{}born\textquotedblright{} (from \emph{zâdan}, \textquotedblleft{}to give birth\textquotedblright{}), and \emph{gâh}, \textquotedblleft{}place\textquotedblright{}: the place one was born. Both are inherited; \emph{gâh} is usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{gāh}.
\end{cousinweb}
